intro.text: The first planet of the Drominad system, usually just called Drominad by the rest of the cosmere. It has one moon and holds a perpendicularity.

The first planet of the Drominad system, usually called Drominad by outsiders, and home to the Eelakin. It holds a perpendicularity, and its Aviar, birds that grant their owners talents, have made it a target for more technologically advanced worlds.

description.text: The homeisles are a group of islands where the Eelakin have built their cities; the more remote ones, far from the capital, are known as the outer isles. Compared with the Pantheon their wildlife is tame and the land well kept, food such as fish is easier to come by, and people keep dogs.

Patji is thought the deadliest island of the Pantheon. Predators from land and sea prowl its beaches, many finding prey by sensing minds, and the jungle inland, barely safer, holds deathants, Cakoban's fingers and tokkas. Nearly blind and deaf nightmaws rule as top predators by tracking minds. The safest spots are near roosting Aviar, which can often hide the minds around them.
South of the homeisles lies the mainland, a frozen waste with no known trace that people ever lived there, though ravens are native to it.

The Pantheon, about forty islands some three weeks' row from the homeisles, looks from afar much like the gentle homeisles but is far deadlier. Some islands have sheltered, gently sloping beaches; others, Patji among them, have steep, rocky shores. The Eelakin have long held the islands holy, yet as their technology grew they began to industrialise them.

items.text: The Eelakin came to this world after a journey through the Cognitive Realm. Their stories speak of empires and great wars, but which world they left is unknown.

They were led by Cakoban the Navigator. Finding the perpendicularity, they passed through into the Pantheon and tamed the Aviar. Cakoban and a few others set out once more and came upon the Dakwara. In time most Eelakin moved from the Pantheon to the homeisles, while some seem to have stayed on as trappers.

An ancient record kept on the Iriali Long Trail tells of the Iriali visiting the planet as a possible new homeland, and mentions a perpendicularity, a deadly island, birds and bugs. When they came is unknown.

Silverlight records tell of expeditions that found a well of power in Shadesmar and passed through it twice or so, never to return; when they set out is unknown. Few knew of these journeys, and many Silverlight arcanists doubted the perpendicularity was real.

As other worlds advanced, the Aviar and the perpendicularity made the planet a prize. The first outsiders were the Malwish, whom the Eelakin called the Ones Above; they had stumbled on the world in the Cognitive Realm first. Interplanetary law barred them from taking it by force, so they offered medicine and new technology as gifts, hoping to advance the Eelakin past that protection. Seeing this, President Vathi slowed the pace to what the islands could support.
Other outsiders followed. The Malwish of Scadrial and the Skybreakers of Roshar both vied for control, each trying to force the Eelakin into an alliance.

Over eight years the Eelakin came to rely on Malwish technology, medicine and power, and the Malwish stirred unrest, such as by delaying power shipments, to press their demands. To stay free, the Eelakin sent explorers into Shadesmar to seek allies. The first expedition failed, but the second, the lone trapper Sixth of the Dusk, rediscovered the ancient Eelakin art of Navigation and came home with the Dakwara, which now helps guard the perpendicularity, and allies from Silverlight.

With their independence firmer, the Eelakin began training new Navigators to guide ships through unmapped parts of the Cognitive Realm, a hugely valuable skill they planned to rent out. Xisisrefliel, a dragon of Silverlight, agreed to spread word of the Navigators and gave the Eelakin translation devices, lodestars, information and a route to and from Silverlight, in return for first right to negotiate lower tariffs. The Eelakin also began building infrastructure for an influx of foreign ships.
